messages: maria: Quick design check 12 I'm experimenting with a 'ghost lineage' visual in the rollout timeline to show forks vs linear version history. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/rollout-timeline#node-id=123. Can people scan for clarity and a11y pitfalls? owen: Visual looks clear at a glance. Concern: users might read the ghost line as an active merge. Could we surface a micro-label on focus/hover like 'forked from v3.1'? maria: Hover labels are in the spec, but hover isn't enough for keyboard/SR users. Sam any guidance? sam: If the line communicates structure it must have a text alternative. Make each node focusable and expose a succinct description: e.g., 'v3.2 12 forked from v3.1 12 20% traffic'. Use roles so screen readers can treat the timeline as a list/collection. Also avoid relying on color alone. devin: Implementation idea: nodes as with aria-describedby pointing to an sr-only span. Example: ```html Forked from v3.1, 20% traffic ``` That should let focus announce details without cluttering the DOM visually. chloe: Performance note 12 some enterprise customers have ~200 versions. Rendering 200 sr-only spans eagerly might bloat the DOM. Can we lazy-render the described span on focus or virtualize the timeline? sam: Agreed. Suggest a collapsed summary that reads like '20 versions 12 use arrow keys to navigate' and only instantiate per-node descriptions when focused or when the user expands that segment. Use an aria-live polite region for expansions so SR users know context changed. maria: Visual tweak: ghost line is 35% opacity in the mock. Since it conveys relationships, increase weight or use a dashed pattern to differentiate forks vs straight ancestry — don't rely on color/opacity alone. owen: Keyboard order: DOM order must match visual left-to-right. For wrapped rows ensure logical order for Tab/arrow navigation. devin: I'll prototype keyboard interactions: left/right arrow to move, Enter/Space to open detail panel. Announce via a single live region: 'v3.2 focused 12 forked from v3.1, 20% traffic'. Will wire lazy DOM creation for the sr-only text. chloe: I'll run perf sims with 50/100/200 nodes and compare eager vs lazy sr nodes. If virtualization is needed, it impacts animation timing and focus management so let's decide early. sam: Once there's a prototype I'll test NVDA + VoiceOver and check that quick arrowing doesn't overwhelm the live region. Also validate the focus ring is visible when themes are high-contrast. maria: Action items: devin -> build keyboard+a11y prototype; sam -> SR testing; chloe -> perf validation and virtualization feasibility. Sync tomorrow 11:00am PT. Thanks :thumbsup:
